page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. Cache hierarchy details include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache pool. The instance is paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory profile of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent with zero GPUs, and no local temporary storage is bundled, making the instance reliant on network-attached storage such as Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced multi-core throughput alongside modest single-threaded performance. Single-core tests, such as Geekbench (1,155.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,411.98), measure in the lower quartile, constrained by the 2.6 GHz clock rate and absence of aggressive single-core boosting. Conversely, multi-threaded tests scale steadily into the middle quartile, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,610.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8,527.6. Memory throughput is solid, recording 44.87 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 32.6 GB/sec for writes, which translates to competitive in-memory throughput, including 6.84 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.85 GB/sec static web throughput.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D8s_v4 delivers balanced resource allocation without the added expense of onboard NVMe drives or accelerator hardware. The trade-off is reliance on external storage and restrained single-thread speed. This architecture fits multi-threaded web serving, caching layers, software compilation runners, and mid-sized database management systems that require predictable multi-core performance.
description: Microsoft Azure D8s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 2.6 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM to deliver a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration excludes onboard local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote volumes such as Premium Storage for disk IO. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-core processing with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,610 and PassMark CPU score of 8,527.6, contrasting with lower-tier single-threaded speeds. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 44.87 GB/s, supporting stable performance in memory-centric workloads. With Redis benchmark throughput of 6.84 million operations per second and solid web serving metrics, the D8s_v4 is well suited for web backends, caching services, software build farms, and standard enterprise applications.
